decision.trend: The trend in the research is to develop high-entropy alloys (HEAs) with improved strength and ductility. Various processing techniques such as vacuum induction melting, directional solidification, and laser powder bed fusion have been used to produce HEAs with unique microstructures. The addition of elements such as Hf, Mo, and Ti has been shown to enhance the mechanical properties of HEAs. The use of computational screening and machine learning models has also been explored to predict the properties of HEAs and guide the design of new alloys.
decision.unsolved: One of the major challenges in the development of HEAs is the trade-off between strength and ductility. Many HEAs exhibit high strength but low ductility, while others show good ductility but lower strength. The development of HEAs that can simultaneously achieve high strength and ductility remains a significant challenge.
decision.why: The use of machine learning models has shown promise in predicting the properties of HEAs and guiding the design of new alloys. By developing a new computational method or potential, researchers can better understand the relationships between the composition, microstructure, and properties of HEAs, and design new alloys that can simultaneously achieve high strength and ductility.
